steps.clueRiddle:
Wheels roll east on a road called four-oh-one.
Play while we drive — the race has begun!
steps.clueReveal: Buckle up for a two-hour drive to Kingston. Play the Kingston trivia deck. Then stamp your 401 East bingo card.

challenges.title: Kingston Trivia Deck
challenges.instructions: Answer questions about today's city. Big cards, one question at a time. Streaks light a little fire.

challenges.title: 401 East Bingo
challenges.instructions: Look out the window for each square. Tap it when you spot it. Four in a row is bingo.

steps.funFact: Highway 401 is the busiest highway in all of North America.

steps.clueRiddle:
Warm and flaky with sugar on top.
Find me first at the morning stop.
steps.clueReveal: Go to Bread & Butter Bakery on Bath Road. Choose any pastry you like. Rate it, then guess what is inside.

challenges.title: Pastry Detective
challenges.instructions: Pick a pastry and take a big bite. What do you think is inside? Rate it, then check every ingredient you guess.
challenges.photoPrompt: Snap a picture of you eating it!

steps.funFact: Kingston is called the Limestone City because so many buildings are grey stone.

steps.clueRiddle:
Stone walls, red coats and one very loud boom.
A goat lives here — can you find him?
steps.clueReveal: Who's ready to be a soldier? Go to Fort Henry on Fort Henry Drive. March, count the cannons, and learn the fort's secrets.

challenges.title: Guard Drill
challenges.instructions: Join the drill, or march like a guard yourself. Stand tall and swing your arms. Keep marching for 30 seconds.

challenges.title: Cannon Count
challenges.instructions: Walk the walls and look for cannons. Count every single one you see. Type your number in the box.

challenges.title: Soldier's Test
challenges.instructions: You can find these answers at the fort. Ask a guard if you get stuck. Three questions to earn your stripes.

trivia.q: What year was the fort you are standing in finished?
trivia.funFact: This is the second Fort Henry — the first one was made of wood.

trivia.q: What colour are the Fort Henry Guard's coats?
trivia.funFact: British soldiers wore red so smoke would not hide them in battle.

trivia.q: What animal is the mascot of the Fort Henry Guard?
trivia.funFact: The mascot goat is always named David, no matter which goat it is.

steps.funFact: Fort Henry was built to guard the Rideau Canal, and no enemy ever attacked it.

steps.clueRiddle:
Thousands of stories stand side by side.
On Princess Street they wait inside.
steps.clueReveal: Walk to Novel Idea at 156 Princess Street. Hunt for six special books.

challenges.title: Book Hunt
challenges.instructions: Find each kind of book on the list. Tap to check it off. Put every book back where it was.
checklist: A book with a boat on the cover
A book with your first initial in the title
A book with an animal on the cover
A book bigger than your own hand

steps.funFact: At an independent bookshop, real people choose every book by hand.

steps.clueRiddle:
Water sprays and swings fly high
right where the lake meets the sky.
steps.clueReveal: Drive to Lake Ontario Park on King Street West. Do the whole playground circuit. Keep playing for 5 minutes.

challenges.title: Playground Circuit
challenges.instructions: Go down the slide once. Then swing ten big swings. Finish with 5 minutes of playing.

steps.funFact: Lake Ontario is the smallest Great Lake, but it is still very deep.

steps.clueRiddle:
A small brown coin gave this place its name.
Two doors from the books, dinner is the game.
steps.clueReveal: Go to Copper Penny at 240 Princess Street. Order dinner with your team. Play trivia while you wait for food.

challenges.title: Dinner Table Trivia
challenges.instructions: Three questions about everything you did today. No looking things up. Just remember your day.

trivia.q: What animal is the Fort Henry mascot?
trivia.funFact: Every mascot goat at Fort Henry is called David.

trivia.q: What did you eat at Bread & Butter Bakery this morning?
trivia.funFact: Bakeries open very early — the bread starts baking before sunrise.

trivia.q: Which big lake did you play beside this afternoon?
trivia.funFact: Kingston sits where Lake Ontario pours into the St. Lawrence River.

steps.funFact: Kingston was the very first capital city of Canada, way back in 1841.

steps.clueRiddle:
Benson Street holds tonight's soft landing.
Run to the mat — leg one is done!
steps.clueReveal: Drive to Comfort Suites at 33 Benson Street. Check in and find your room. Then step onto the pit stop mat.
steps.funFact: In the real race, the last team to reach the mat may be eliminated.
